title: Focus cascade playbook and failure-mode matrix (working)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working playbook to translate the company-level focus into a two-week execution cadence leading into the Q2 all-hands. Primary outcomes: (1) a compact, prioritized OKR slate for exec review; (2) a decision grid for tradeoffs during peak-week; (3) a failure-mode matrix with clear mitigations and owners. This is intentionally terse — treat as the team’s operating checklist until the formal runbook is published.

Context / why now:
- We have three overlapping demands: Dedicated capacity commercial launch, Private deployment compliance backlog, and a set of serving-runtime regressions flagged by SRE.
- Senior leadership wants a short, defensible OKR set for the next quarter by the executive sync on 2026-02-27.
- We will use the all-hands as the public-facing alignment moment; the internal rollout (team-level kickoffs) will follow the all-hands by 48–72 hours.

Top-level proposed OKR candidates (working list):
- Objective A: Make production inference predictable and 30% cheaper for mid-tail workloads
  - KR A1: Reduce median cost/token for 512-token workload by 20% (benchmarks across 3 models)
  - KR A2: Ship auto-batching tuning to 80% of production lanes
  - KR A3: 2% or fewer inference time regressions (monthly ROIs)

- Objective B: Enterprise readiness for Private (first regulated customer)
  - KR B1: KMS + HSM integration validated end-to-end (pen test signoff)
  - KR B2: Private control plane stability: 99.9% uptime during smoke test window
  - KR B3: On-prem packaging and installer docs for two common infra patterns

- Objective C: Developer adoption velocity (platform stickiness)
  - KR C1: 30% uplift in weekly active SDK users on new docs/playbooks
  - KR C2: Complete three PLG templates for vector search + reranking

Decision grid (how we pick what to commit):
- Columns: Impact to units (high/med/low), Complexity (high/med/low), Cross-team dependency (many/few), Risk of regressions (high/med/low), Time to value (days).
- Rule of thumb: For company OKRs, prefer high impact / low complexity / low cross-team dependency items first. Items with high risk but high impact must have a clear rollback path before committing.

Failure-mode matrix (candidate entries; quick reference):
- Failure: Dedicated capacity launch exceeds latency SLOs on p95
  - Trigger: p95 drift > 20% for 2 hours in staging or pilot region
  - Immediate mitigation: Re-route new traffic to hosted API isolated pool; throttle non-critical customers; open incident channel #infra-dedicated
  - Owner: Diego Alvarez
  - Recovery yardstick: p95 back within 10% of baseline within 60 minutes

- Failure: KMS/HSM integration causes deployment block for Private customers
  - Trigger: Key rotation failure on first smoke test deploy
  - Immediate mitigation: Fallback to ephemeral encryption keys for test tenants; apply gating in installer; notify sales ops and legal with templated messaging
  - Owner: Rina Patel
  - Recovery yardstick: Successful deploy with HSM or approved fallback documented within 48 hours

- Failure: Serving runtime regression creates >1% token-level error rate for long-context models
  - Trigger: automated regression detector flags spike in token errors
  - Immediate mitigation: Roll back to previous runtime build in canary lanes; pause rollout; start triage with serving-runtime and SRE
  - Owner: Tom Keller
  - Recovery yardstick: rollback complete and error rate <0.5% within 30 minutes

Run-of-show for the all-hands (compact format):
- 00:00–00:04 Opening (CEO) — 1 slide: northstar + single-line company commitment for the quarter (prep note: keep language simple)
- 00:04–00:14 Product demo & highlights — 3 slides each: Hosted API wins, Dedicated pilot story, Private delivery milestones (speakers: Product leads + SE)
- 00:14–00:22 Ops & reliability update — 2 slides: SLO progress and key mitigations (speaker: SRE lead)
- 00:22–00:30 OKR announcement and what we’re asking teams to do — 2 slides + 1 slide with top 5 tactical asks (speaker: COO)
- 00:30–00:40 Q&A / townline: pre-seeded questions + live (moderator: People Ops)

Communication assets to prepare before exec sync:
- One-pager (for execs): top 3 OKRs, primary risks, contingency triggers — 1 page (owner: Maya)
- Slide pack (for all-hands): 8–10 slides; export script for accessibility (owner: Claire)
- Readout email to staff: short TL;DR + three team-level actions + links to playbook (owner: People Ops lead - assign)

Immediate action items (next 7 days):
- Monday: freeze OKR candidates; exec pre-read sent (Maya)
- Tuesday: tabletop simulation for failure modes w/ SRE and Platform (Tom, Diego)
- Wednesday: finalize all-hands run-of-show and rehearse 1x with execs (Claire)
- Thursday: publish external-facing FAQ for customers on Dedicated launch window (SE)
- Friday: consolidate team kickoff templates and route to managers (Rina)

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs (notes to self):
- Do we include a cost-driven KR that explicitly ties to customer TCO? Pros: clear business metric. Cons: might push premature quantization choices that hurt quality.
- Should we prioritize a single cross-functional epic to reduce context-switching? Which epic yields the best unit economics per engineer-week? Need data from finance.
- Hiring asks: one infra reliability IC for Q2 — can recruiting guarantee 12-week start? If no, plan fallback to contractor with ramp mentor.

Stakeholder matrix (short):
- Execs: CEO (narrative), COO (operational commitments), CFO (cost KRs)
- Critical teams: serving-runtime (latency & regressions), dedicated (capacity), private (security & packaging), SRE (SLOs), Solutions Eng & Sales (customer-facing readiness)

Notes on tone and framing for all-hands:
- Treat the all-hands as an alignment signal, not a feature launch party. Avoid heavy engineering detail in the main stage; reserve technical walkthroughs for office hours and deep-dive sessions.
- Frame risks candidly with mitigation steps; people respond better to honest confidence vs. glossing over.

Appendix — quick templates (copy/paste in emails):
- Exec pre-read subject: "[Pre-read] Q2 Focus Candidates & Risk Triggers — please review by EOD Tue"
- Readout email TL;DR: "This quarter we prioritize predictable, economical inference, enterprise readiness for Private, and developer adoption. Teams: see 3 asks below. Townline + Q&A at HH. Full playbook: <link>"

Working draft sign-off:
- Draft owner: Maya Ortiz (please comment inline; use the linked doc for tracked edits)
- Next review: Exec pre-read version due 2026-02-24 (owner: Maya)

Quick reference: emergency channels & escalation ladder:
- Slack incident channel: #incident-ops (ping rotation: on-call SRE)
- Pager duty: infra-pd (primary: Diego, backup: Tom)
- Exec escalation: COO -> CEO (if customer-impacting outage > 60 minutes)

End of working draft. This doc will be iterated and split into the formal runbook + slide pack. Keep comments inline and tag owners for quick resolutions.
